title: Acme Bio — LLM migration parity walkthrough
summary: Redwood demo focused on migration parity from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood API. Covered model mapping, streaming and function-calling differences, embedding parity, SDK changes, console rollout and Optimize recommendations for batching/caching. Customer concerns: PHI handling, KMS, SSO, latency targets. Agreed next steps: share benchmark script, provide trial keys, schedule security deep-dive and pilot kickoff.
topics: SDK migration snippets and minimal code changes
Console: model pinning, canary rollouts, cost/latency dashboards
Optimize: batching, KV caching, quantization recommendations
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-03-12 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48m
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Ben (Redwood), Jordan (Acme ML), Maya (Prod), Samir (Security), Tina (CTO)

00:00 Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Alex, AE for Redwood Inference, Priya is our SE, Ben's on solutions. How's everyone doing?
00:12 Jordan (Acme): Good thanks. Excited to see the migration plan, we've been talking about moving away from OpenAI for some workloads.
00:18 Priya (SE): Awesome. Today's agenda is practical parity mapping — how you go from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together calls to Redwood with minimal code changes, what the console gives you for rollout + observe, and some Optimize suggestions for cost/latency.
00:35 Maya (Product): Sounds good. Main concern is parity on outputs and latency — especially for live annotation flows.
00:42 Priya (SE): Totally. We'll demo examples where we keep temperature/top_p, function-calling, streaming, and embeddings behavior aligned.
00:52 Ben: Also we'll show how Model Catalog maps common names — e.g., gpt-4-ish -> rwd-xlarge, claude-like -> rwd-clarion, and Together models to the specific quantized variants. These are example mappings — you can pin exact model versions.
01:12 Jordan: Quick question — do you keep the same tokenization? We have pipelines that rely on token counts for billing and truncation.
01:22 Priya (SE): Good point. Tokenization differences exist across models; we provide a tokenization shim in the SDK that will report token counts consistent with the chosen model. For migration, we recommend running the tokenizer on a representative prompt set to compare. We'll share the script.
01:45 Samir (Security): For us the top blocker is PHI — we need guarantees for data in transit and at rest, KMS integration, and audit logs. Also SSO and RBAC.
01:56 Alex (AE): Short answer: we support customer-managed KMS, SOC 2 compliance, audit logs, SAML/SSO, and Private deployments (VPC/on-prem). We'll surface links to our compliance pack after the call. We'll also put together a security deep-dive.
02:12 Priya (SE): Ok jumping into a demo — I'll share my screen.
02:20 [screen share starts]
02:30 Priya (SE): This is our API quickstart. First, a simple generative call: we accept a request body similar to OpenAI's, with model, messages, temperature, max_tokens. Endpoint differences: /v1/generate vs /v1/chat/completions — but our SDK wrappers let you call the same function names with minimal changes.
03:01 Jordan: So code swap is tiny?
03:05 Priya (SE): For many teams yes. Example: OpenAI call -- client.chat.completions.create({model: 'gpt-4', messages: [...]}) vs Redwood's client.responses.create({model: 'rwd-xlarge', input: messages}) — we provide a compatibility shim that accepts messages and translates. We'll paste snippet.
03:30 Maya: What about streaming? We rely on token streaming for UX.
03:35 Priya (SE): We support chunked streaming via server-sent events and websocket; semantics are similar. One caveat: some Together models stream at different chunk sizes due to different decoding internals, so you may see slightly different chunk boundaries but final text parity should be comparable.
03:55 Jordan: Function-calling — our assistants use JSON-schema function calls from OpenAI. Does Redwood support that?
04:02 Priya (SE): Yes, function-calling is supported. We have a function call layer that maps to model-native function features or emulates them if the model doesn't support native function calling. For migration we recommend keeping your function schemas; Redwood will route and either use native function call or return a structured object with the call intent. There are a couple of edge cases around streaming function results — we'll point those out in the migration doc.
04:32 Ben: I'll show the Console. Here you can pin model versions, set rollout policies (percent traffic canary), and define fallback chains. If a selected model is unavailable we can fallback to a smaller quantized variant or a hosted alternative.
05:00 Priya (SE): Also the Console shows token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route which helps when you map your OpenAI usage. You can see cost per token by model and by route.
05:18 Maya: Nice. We need to know expected latency for rwd-xlarge vs our current gpt-4 setup.
05:25 Priya (SE): Our public benchmarks indicate rwd-xlarge at ~120ms per token on A100 for synthesis workloads at 128 seq, but real numbers vary by prompt length and batch. For your interactive flows we'd recommend running a 24–72 hour benchmark with your prompt set. We'll help run that.
05:45 Jordan: About embeddings — we use OpenAI text-embedding-3-large for 1536 dims. How does Redwood handle embeddings sizes and similarity?
05:54 Priya (SE): We have embeddings catalog and parity models. If you need 1536 dims we map to a 1536 embedding family; if the model differs, we recommend re-embedding or running a conversion check. For semantic similarity we provide evaluation harnesses.
06:18 Samir (Security): Where are embeddings stored by default? We need data residency and auto-delete policies.
06:25 Alex (AE): Hosted retains embeddings only as configured; we can disable retention for customer data or you can use Private deployment where nothing leaves your VPC. We support retention TTLs and purge APIs.
06:36 Priya (SE): Now code examples — here's JS shim: 1) change import to @redwood/inference, 2) call client.responses.stream or .create; most of your logic around messages and function schemas stays the same. For Python same idea. We'll share a migration gist.
07:05 Jordan: Do you have a list of exact parameter mappings for temperature/top_p/presence_penalty etc? We have automation setting those values.
07:12 Priya (SE): Yes — mapping doc will have parameter equivalences. Some colliding params may be no-ops on certain model families; we'll flag those.
07:26 Ben: Optimize suggestions — here's an example route where we took your prompt set and suggested batching at 8 with KV cache enabled for common prefixes, cutting token costs by ~30% with near-identical latency. Optimize also suggests quantization profiles per model when high throughput is needed.
07:55 Jordan: Explain KV cache briefly — we have a lot of repeated prefixes.
08:00 Priya (SE): KV cache keeps cached key-value transformer states for repeated prefixes so subsequent requests with the same prefix skip recomputing early layers; it's safe for deterministic prompts and reduces compute significantly. Our SDK will manage cache keys and invalidation.
08:24 Maya: Any config required in-app?
08:28 Priya (SE): Mostly policy settings in Redwood Console and small client options. We'll show sample config later.
08:36 Samir (Security): Let's talk encryption — customer-managed KMS? HSM?
08:41 Alex (AE): We integrate with AWS KMS and GCP KMS and HSMs for Private; hosted customers can use a customer-managed key. For PCI/PHI we recommend Private deployment with our audit bundle. We'll attach the compliance pack.
08:58 Priya (SE): Now I'll run a short live migration demo — small Node snippet converting an OpenAI chat call to Redwood.
09:05 [screen: code editor]
09:12 Priya (SE): Original OpenAI: await openai.chat.completions.create({model:'gpt-4', messages}) -> returns choices[0].message.content. New Redwood: const resp = await client.responses.create({model:'rwd-xlarge', input: messages}); const text = resp.output[0].content[0].text; The shim can return OpenAI-like shape if you enable compatibility mode.
09:45 Jordan: That helps. Any behavioral drift expected?
09:49 Priya (SE): Minor. Different decoder weights, tokenization, or sampling seeds can produce slight phrasing differences. We provide a regression eval harness so you can run your prompt set pre/post and set acceptance thresholds.
10:12 Maya: How do we do canary releases? We want 10% traffic to Redwood for a week.
10:20 Ben: In Console you create a route, pin the new model, set rollout to 10% and choose a fallback to the old provider. You can also add a percent-based or header-based rule for tenant bucketing.
10:38 Samir (Security): Audit logs — do you have per-request lineage? We need to show who invoked what and traceability for calls that process PHI.
10:48 Alex (AE): Yes, per-request logs, with request IDs, user metadata, and model version. In Private deployments logs can be routed to your SIEM.
11:05 Priya (SE): Back to function calling nuance — when migrating from OpenAI's function_call: 'auto' you'll want to ensure your JSON schemas are strict; some models will return slightly different shapes. Redwood's function layer normalizes outputs where possible.
11:25 Jordan: Ok. Let's talk cost modelling. We pay per 1k tokens today to OpenAI; how to estimate Redwood hosted costs?
11:33 Ben: We'll run a cost comparison using your token stats and our model unit pricing. Typically you get savings via batching, KV cache and quantization on Redwood. For high-throughput workloads we recommend Dedicated capacity — predictable monthly commit. We'll send a cost/throughput spreadsheet.
12:00 Priya (SE): Now a quick live demo of Console Optimize tab — it highlights top routes by spend, suggests batching sizes, cache rules and model quantization. Here it flagged two chat routes and suggested a 4-token prefix cache and batch size 6.
12:28 Jordan: For embeddings-heavy jobs — is there a way to incremental-replace a large vector index? We can't re-embed 10M documents at once.
12:36 Priya (SE): We recommend a rolling re-embed pipeline — use the console to create a batch job and throttle to control cost. If dimensions differ we run a compatibility check and provide a conversion plan.
12:52 Maya: Regarding Together — some of our models are proprietary on Together. Can Redwood host Together models or help with quantized variants?
13:01 Ben: We have onboarding for third-party model binaries when licensing permits. For Together-hosted models we can either run them in Dedicated or build a compatible quantized variant — there is some ops work required and a security review.
13:20 Samir (Security): How long is the Private deployment onboarding?
13:24 Alex (AE): Depending on scope 2–8 weeks typical; for full on-prem with HSM integration can be longer. We provide an onboarding checklist.
13:36 Priya (SE): Next I'll show a short benchmark runner we use for parity testing. It runs N parallel clients, measures p50/p95 latency, token throughput, and compares outputs using a similarity metric.
13:54 [screen: benchmark UI]
14:05 Priya (SE): Example run: 1k prompts, batch size 4, rwd-xlarge p50 310ms p95 1.2s under average load. OpenAI gpt-4 in our lab p50 280ms p95 1.1s — close enough for many apps, with lower $/token after Optimize. We'll share the benchmark config.
14:36 Jordan: For regression tests — do you keep model snapshots? We need to pin exact weights for reproducibility.
14:44 Priya (SE): Yes, model versioning is first-class. Console shows the model hash, you can pin to a specific model build and we'll preserve that variant.
15:00 Maya: API keys and secrets — rotating? We want integration with Vault.
:15:06 Alex (AE): Keys rotate and you can integrate Redwood with your Vault for Private deployments. Hosted also has rotation APIs and short-lived tokens.
15:20 Samir (Security): Do you support IP allowlists and egress restrictions?
15:25 Ben: VPC peering and Private options allow strict egress deny and allowlist. Hosted has IP ranges and firewall options.
15:40 Priya (SE): Quick note on telemetry — you can opt-in/out of perf telemetry. For Private, telemetry is optional and can be forwarded to your SIEM.
15:52 Jordan: Anything we need to change in our prompt engineering?
15:57 Priya (SE): Mostly small adjustments. We recommend a pre/post evaluation pass to measure drift on your critical prompts and only adjust if drift exceeds threshold. Our Optimize tool can surface suggested prompt changes.
16:12 Maya: Ok so next steps?
16:15 Alex (AE): We'll recap at the end — but first any blockers?
16:20 Samir (Security): Need SOC2 docs and encryption spec. Also confirm we can do Private with HSM.
16:27 Alex (AE): We'll send compliance pack and outline Private HSM onboarding.
16:32 Jordan: I'd like the benchmark script and a trial key.
16:35 Priya (SE): We'll provide trial keys scoped for a 7–14 day pilot, and the benchmark runner with your prompt set.
16:44 Maya: Pricing for Dedicated vs hosted pilot?
16:47 Ben: Ben: we'll email a comparison spreadsheet with committed throughput tiers and expected unit economics.
16:52 Alex (AE): Great. Any other questions?
17:00 Tina (CTO): One last thing — support SLAs? We need a 24/7 escalation path for production incidents.
17:07 Alex (AE): We offer premium SLA tiers with 2-hour p1 response and 24/7 coverage as an add-on. We'll include SLA language in the follow-up.
17:18 [wrap up]
17:25 Alex (AE): Recap — share migration gist + compatibility shim, benchmark script, trial keys, security pack, pricing spreadsheet, schedule security deep-dive and pilot kickoff.
17:40 Jordan: Thanks all, looking forward to the benchmarks.
17:44 Maya: Appreciate the demo.
17:48 Priya (SE): Thanks everyone.
17:52 [call ends]
